title: The Army of Elephants and the Ababil Birds
summary: The story of the army of elephants that wanted to destroy the Ka'bah, and the Ababil birds that Allah sent to guard it. (QS. Al-Fil)
moral: Allah is All-Powerful in guarding His house. Strength and arrogance mean nothing before Him.
pages: In the city of Mecca, surrounded by desert, stood the Ka'bah, the noble house of Allah. People from many places came to honour it.
One day, Abrahah, a ruler from Yemen, came with a great army of elephants. He was envious and determined to destroy the Ka'bah. The ground trembled and dust billowed into the sky.
The people of Mecca withdrew to the hills. Their leader said, 'This Ka'bah has an Owner who will guard it.' So they waited in full confidence.

When the army was about to advance, the largest elephant suddenly stopped. It would not step toward the Ka'bah. Though it was struck and coaxed, it stayed still, while the other elephants were confused.
Suddenly the sky filled with small birds coming in flocks. They were the Ababil birds, and each carried a small stone of hard clay.
The birds dropped their stones. The army of elephants was thrown into chaos and fled in disarray. Allah made them like leaves eaten by caterpillars.
The Ka'bah stood safe. That event happened in the year known as the Year of the Elephant. We learn that the arrogant will never win against the will of Allah. The end.
